summary: Julius Dutoit worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Adalbert Kuhn and under Ernst Kuhn around 1894–1898.

Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as an honorary professor at the University of Strasbourg and director of its National and University Library (1900–1909).

Julius Grill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the universities of Tübingen and Jena under Adalbert Kuhn and Rudolf von Roth, and later served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen from 1888 to 1913.
Julius Hoffory was a linguist who studied at the universities of Copenhagen, Strasbourg, and Berlin. He later held a post at the University of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1893.

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Munich, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He served as a professor at the University of Würzburg (1877–1920) and Tagore Professor at Calcutta.

Julius Lipner is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Jnana Deepa, Jadavpur, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis, and served as Professor of Hinduism and Comparative Religion at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and sinology. He studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy, Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at Tübingen (1826–1834) and the Collège de France (1847–1876).
Julius Pokorny was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much. He held academic posts at Vienna, Berlin (circa 1920–1935), Bern, and Zurich.
Julius Schubring worked in history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at the universities of Göttingen, Bonn, and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg.

Julius Zupitza was a linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Moriz Haupt. He held academic appointments at the universities of Breslau (circa 1869–1872), Vienna (circa 1872–1876), and Berlin (circa 1876–1895).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from circa 2010 to 2013.

Jun Takashima is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and later held appointments as an assistant professor at Aichi Prefectural University and professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2020).

Jundo Nagashima works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and Paul Williams, earning a PhD from the University of Bristol, and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2013–2017).

June McDaniel is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed degrees at Emory University and the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston, where she was attested between 2000 and 2015.

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, later working as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history and archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Ha studied at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and completed a PhD at Duke University under the supervision of Stanley Abe.

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, and Leipzig under Max Müller and Sylvain Lévi. He served as professor and president of the University of Tokyo and rector of Toyo University.
Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Toyo University and later served as a professor at both Toyo University and Komazawa University.

Junkichi Imanishi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Hokkaido University, was Chancellor of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
